summary.text: Joy Garratt is a Democratic state representative from District 29 who has represented the district since 2019 and is seeking re-election in the New Mexico House of Representatives in the November 3, 2026 general election.
Garratt is a former classroom teacher whose legislative work has focused on education and workforce development.

paragraphs.text: Joy Garratt was born in Long Beach, California.

She earned a B.S. in liberal studies from Excelsior College, a master's degree in educational leadership from the University of New Mexico, and a post-baccalaureate teacher license from the university.

In a 2024 Ballotpedia survey, she said she taught K-12 students for more than 28 years, including in South Korea, California and Connecticut, and spent her last 12 years teaching in Albuquerque Public Schools.
Ballotpedia also lists work in public affairs and public relations.
Garratt took office in the New Mexico House on January 1, 2019.
For 2025-2026 she is listed on the Appropriations and Finance, Commerce and Economic Development, House Education, and Rules and Order of Business committees, serving as vice chair of the last two.

She said in the 2024 survey that she has sponsored bills on apprenticeship funding, educator salaries, teacher residencies and adult-student scholarships, and that she has also worked on road infrastructure, public safety and health insurance coverage for biomarker testing.
